concept: Trotterized quantum chemistry ansatzes can violate expected chemical properties
summary: Low-order or poorly controlled Trotterization can introduce large numerical differences and property violations in quantum chemistry workflows, including orbital-sensitivity and size-consistency issues.
limitations: The concern is application-sensitive; it does not imply all Trotterized quantum chemistry workflows fail.
Mitigations can include localized orbitals, controlled decomposition choices, additional Trotter steps, or exact small-system benchmarking.
implications: Do not recommend low-order Trotterization blindly for size-consistency-sensitive chemistry tasks.
Ask for molecular orbital convention, accuracy target, and whether size consistency matters.
Use exact evolution on small fragments or benchmark systems when feasible.

evidence.note: Reports large differences between Trotterized UCCSD wavefunctions and questions chemical well-definedness.
Discusses size-consistency and orbital-invariance issues in VQE-UCCSD calculations.
Studies size consistency in QPE full-CI with Trotter decomposition.
